groups.title: Shared Zod schemas across client and server
groups.question: Your sign-up form checks that a username is at least 3 characters, but the server allows 2, and users get confusing errors. Explain how you would share validation between client and server.

followUps.Why sharing schemas eliminates client-se: How does sharing one Zod schema prevent client and server from disagreeing?
followUps.Zod's refinement and transform methods f: When would you use refine and when transform in a Zod schema?

evidence.text: One schema is imported by both the tRPC procedure and the form.
Both sides then enforce exactly the same rules.
Changing a rule in the schema updates validation everywhere at once.

notEnough: Only saying you reuse the schema.

evidence.text: refine adds a custom check with its own error message.
transform changes the value while parsing, for example trimming spaces.
Because the schema is shared, these run the same way on client and server.

notEnough: Only saying they add custom logic.

groups.title: React Hook Form architecture: uncontrolled inputs with a single re-render
groups.question: A large form with twenty fields lags on every keystroke. Explain how React Hook Form avoids this.

followUps.Why RHF uses refs instead of state to av: Why doesn't React Hook Form re-render the form on every keystroke?

evidence.text: React Hook Form keeps input values in refs, not React state.
Typing does not cause the form component to re-render.
It re-renders only when needed, such as on submit, on errors or for watched fields.

notEnough: Only saying React Hook Form is faster.

groups.title: Wiring React Hook Form with Zod and tRPC
groups.question: You are wiring a create-post form with React Hook Form, a Zod schema and a tRPC mutation. Explain how the pieces connect from typing to submitting.

followUps.register, handleSubmit, and formState.er: What do register, handleSubmit and formState.errors each do?

evidence.text: zodResolver connects a Zod schema to React Hook Form.
On submit the form values are checked against the schema.
Schema errors are mapped to the matching fields without manual validation code.

notEnough: Only saying it uses Zod for validation.

evidence.text: register connects an input to the form with its name and change handlers.
handleSubmit validates the form and calls your function only with valid, typed data.
formState.errors holds the messages to show next to each field.

groups.title: Accessible form UI and user feedback patterns
groups.question: Screen reader users submit your form and do not know which fields have errors, and users click save twice because nothing tells them it worked. Explain how you would give clear feedback.

followUps.Associating error messages with inputs f: How do you make sure a screen reader announces a field's error?
followUps.Optimistic toast notifications with reac: How would toast notifications show the progress of a save?

evidence.text: The input points to its error message with aria-describedby.
Screen readers read the error when the input gets focus.
Marking the input as invalid also tells assistive tools that it has a problem.

notEnough: Only saying errors should be accessible.

evidence.text: A loading toast appears when the save starts.
It is replaced with a success or error message when the request settles.
Clear feedback stops users from clicking again because they think nothing happened.

notEnough: Only saying you would show a toast.
